title: Data and code for: Evapotranspiration of Persistent Florida Citrus Groves during the Huanglongbing Era: Sensitivity to Reference Evapotranspiration and Links to Canopy and Soil Water Storage

creators.name: Rodrigues, Hugo
creators.affiliation: Range Cattle Research and Education Center, Institute of Food and Agricultural Sciences, University of Florida

description: Scripts, derived data and figures that reproduce every number, table and figure of the article "Evapotranspiration of Persistent Florida Citrus Groves during the Huanglongbing Era: Sensitivity to Reference Evapotranspiration and Links to Canopy and Soil Water Storage", submitted to Land (MDPI), Special Issue "Monitoring and Modelling the Water and Carbon Dynamics in the Soil-Plant-Atmosphere Continuum". The archive reconstructs 2000-2025 OpenET v2.1 evapotranspiration for 1698 one-kilometre cells (87,225 ha) of persistent Florida citrus groves under four reference evapotranspiration scenarios (raw and bias-corrected gridMET; FAWN station ET0 with measured and with standardized wind), with validation at the USGS citrus ET tower near Arcadia, hurricane wind exposure from HURDAT2, a comparison with the historical UF/IFAS crop coefficients, a NAIP canopy index and gNATSGO soil water storage. Google Earth Engine inputs are not redistributed; their identifiers are given in README.md and in the scripts. WORKFLOW.md describes each script and the order of execution.
